refutation_attempt: Read every effect renderer's BindTexture/BindTextureCube/BindTexture3D and the null-returning cube factories. Every backend tolerates the null pointer; the only null-returning renderers with effects (DirectX9, FNA3D) inherit a no-op bind; Texture3D's constructor already refuses; Texture2D shares the disposed case.
reason: Disposal leaves an empty shared_ptr that SetTexture dereferences (formally undefined) and CNA elsewhere throws ObjectDisposedException, so a low bug survives. But no crash path exists (null is ignored), the disposed case hits the Texture2D overload equally, and a storage-less Texture3D cannot be constructed.

correction.title: ShaderEffect::SetTexture(int, Texture2D&), SetTexture(int, TextureCube&) and SetTexture(int, Texture3D&) evaluate *renderer_ of a disposed texture (an empty shared_ptr) and forward a null pointer instead of throwing ObjectDisposedException
correction.summary: All three SetTexture overloads pass &texture.GetRenderer(), and GetRenderer() returns *renderer_. Dispose resets renderer_, so a disposed texture yields a reference formed from an empty shared_ptr (formally undefined behaviour) and a null pointer reaches IEffectRenderer::BindTexture, BindTextureCube or BindTexture3D.
correction.expected: CNA's convention for consuming a disposed resource is System::ObjectDisposedException (SpriteBatch::Draw, GraphicsDevice texture and buffer binding, and ShaderEffect::SetTextureArrayEXT, whose header documents the throw). SetTexture should refuse a disposed texture the same way instead of forming a reference from an empty shared_ptr.
correction.actual: modules/graphics/src/Xna/ShaderEffect.cpp binds &texture.GetRenderer() for Texture2D, TextureCube and Texture3D, and each of their Dispose overrides resets renderer_. Every renderer that overrides these binds tolerates the resulting null pointer: EasyGL and OpenGL4 return early, WebGPU and SDL_GPU resolve null to an empty binding, Vulkan, Direct3D 11 and Direct3D 12 dynamic_cast it to null and fall back to a default or empty view. The observable result is a silently unbound sampler slot (an abort only where the standard library is built with assertions), not a crash. The storage-less case is narrow: a TextureCube on DirectX9 without cubemap caps, or an FNA3D creation failure, both of which leave BindTextureCube at the base no-op; Texture3D's constructor already throws NotSupportedException when the capability is missing.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry. Effect tests that bind live cube and volume textures (for example vulkan_effect_bound_texture_test.cpp and easygl_texture3d_addressw_test.cpp) exercise the overloads; none binds a disposed texture.

refutation_attempt: Looked for an override or intermediate base supplying the applied depth format on WEBGPU (none; it derives IGraphicsRenderer directly), traced Clear gating to the echoed value, and checked whether echo is intended: VULKAN-348's comment and test set the contract; WebGPU's own MSAA fix follows it.
reason: WebGPURenderer::RecreateDepthTexture always allocates Depth24PlusStencil8 and no GetAppliedDepthStencilFormatEXT override exists, so PresentationParameters echoes the request. CNA's own VULKAN-348 comment and Vulkan_AppliedFormats define reporting the format in effect as the contract. Stencil gating uses the echoed value, as stated.

refutation_attempt: Searched D3D9 and GraphicsDevice for a caps check, clamp or applied-interval write-back (none). Traced construction (CreateDevice failure throws once) versus Present, EnsureDeviceSize and the failed-Reset branch (size reverted, interval not). Read XNA's PresentInterval docs. Windowed rejection is unexecuted.
reason: The CNA code claims hold for post-construction changes: no caps check, and a failed Reset leaves swapInterval_ at 2 with presentationDirty_ set, so each Present releases default-pool resources and retries. But at construction a rejected value throws once from CreateDevice, so the loop needs a later Reset or SetPresentationParameters. That D3D9 rejects windowed Two is documented, not run here.

correction.actual: modules/renderers/directx9/src/DirectX9Renderer.cpp's BuildPresentParameters switches on the interval with no caps check, so Two becomes D3DPRESENT_INTERVAL_TWO whatever the device or window mode. At construction a rejected value fails once and loudly (CreateDevice throws std::runtime_error). After construction, SetSwapInterval (reached from GraphicsDevice::Reset and SetPresentationParameters) marks the presentation dirty; EnsureDeviceSize (run from every Present) releases every D3DPOOL_DEFAULT resource, calls device_->Reset, and on failure keeps the previous size, leaves the requested interval and presentationDirty_ set and logs 'retrying next frame'. Direct3D 9 documents only DEFAULT, IMMEDIATE and ONE as valid for windowed swap chains, so a windowed device switched to Two after construction (for example by GraphicsDevice::Reset with new PresentationParameters; GraphicsDeviceManager only ever requests One or Immediate) can enter this loop: a warning per frame and default-pool resources released and recreated every frame, with PresentationParameters still claiming Two.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry. The windowed-mode restriction is Direct3D 9's documented behaviour (XNA's PresentInterval documentation likewise guarantees only One and Immediate for windowed swap chains and tells callers to check capabilities for Two), not re-checked on a device; whether Wine/DXVK reject it the same way was not observed, so the retry loop is inferred rather than verified. No DIRECTX9 test requests PresentInterval::Two; the DIRECTX9 tests exercise device creation and Present only.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a post-construction SetSwapInterval in GraphicsDevice's creation path (none; only Reset and SetPresentationParameters forward it), read the present-interval test (Reset only, no accessor for the real vsync) and checked whether the constructor mapping is a deliberate exception; its comment is stale.
reason: The constructor still maps swapInterval > 0 to 1 under a comment that contradicts SetSwapInterval's Task 713 fix and SDL3's documented interval semantics; nothing re-forwards the interval after direct construction. The Game path is masked by Reset, as stated. Test covers Reset only.

refutation_attempt: Traced which Texture2D creation paths consult the device maximum: sized constructors, FromStream and the XNB reader check the profile ceiling (2048/4096) first, protecting 4096- or 8192-limited devices, while the file-path constructor and CreateFromPixels validate nothing. Grepped the repository for a GL size query (none).
reason: The contract mismatch is real: only VULKAN, DIRECT2D and GDI report a real limit, the rest return an unqueried constant marked known. But the interface comment does not say no renderer overrides it, and the profile ceiling guards most Texture2D and RenderTarget2D paths; exposure is via EXT texture types, engine-layer allocations and the unvalidated file-path constructor.

correction.summary: Only VULKAN, DIRECT2D and GDI report a real or bounded limit; the other families inherit a constant 16384 (no code in the repository queries GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE), which the renderer capability profile nevertheless reports as a known limit.
correction.actual: IGraphicsRenderer::GetMaxTextureDimension in modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/IGraphicsRenderer.hpp returns 16384. Its comment justifies the default as the guaranteed ceiling on every native API the project targets and says no renderer currently needs a tighter or looser override; that is stale (VULKAN, DIRECT2D and GDI override) and untrue for GLES, WebGL and Vulkan, whose guarantees are far lower. VULKAN (maxImageDimension2D), DIRECT2D (GetMaximumBitmapSize) and GDI (a fixed software-framebuffer ceiling) override; FNA3D overrides only to return the default because FNA3D has no query. EasyGL, OPENGL4, SDL_GPU, WEBGPU (which holds deviceLimits_.maxTextureDimension2D but does not return it) and the rest inherit 16384. modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp sets RendererLimit::MaxTextureDimension known whenever the value is non-negative. The sized Texture2D constructors, Texture2D::FromStream, the XNB reader and every RenderTarget2D constructor check the GraphicsProfile ceiling (2048 Reach, 4096 HiDef) before the device maximum, so a device limited to 4096 or 8192 is not exposed through them; the CNAEXT file-path constructor Texture2D(assetName, device) and Texture2D::CreateFromPixels perform no size validation at all. The unqueried value reaches the native API through paths that trust the device limit and its known flag: StorageTexture2D and Texture2DArray preparation, engine-layer render-target sizes (EngineLayerTextureSizeScope::MaxRenderTargetSize), and any application that reads the reported value.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading at 009d40f5; not executed. Blast radius is narrower than first written: the sized, stream and content-reader Texture2D paths and RenderTarget2D are bounded by the profile ceiling; the exposure is EXT texture types, engine-layer allocations and callers that treat the reported maximum as the truth on devices whose real limit is below 16384. The unvalidated file-path constructor is a separate missing check that a correct maximum would not fix.

refutation_attempt: Looked for another SDL_GPU custom-effect route or GraphicsDevice guard consuming vertexStreams or refusing multi-stream ShaderEffect draws (none); confirmed the limitation sentence predates SMG-0022 and CNA's own engine-layer doc lists SDL_GPU instancing through custom effects; grepped SDL_GPU examples for instance-frequency bindings (none).
reason: Custom-effect draws build attributes from the first declaration at slot 0 and bind one vertex buffer; other streams are ignored or refused by the location check. refutation_attempt: Enumerated every ISpriteBatchRenderer subclass for a float-destination override (only EasyGL, OPENGL4, SOFTWARE; GDI's wrapper forwards only integer overloads), checked SpriteBatch passes floats, and searched for renderer-level sub-pixel tests, finding a renderer-neutral pixel fixture the entry does not mention.
reason: The gap holds: the float overload's documented default truncates and only three renderers override it. But the tests text is wrong: spritebatch_subpixel_contract_test.cpp (SOFTWARE-137), a byte-exact renderer-neutral pixel fixture that a truncating renderer fails, is registered for EasyGL, OPENGL4 and SOFTWARE, so it does check what those draw.

correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry. The set of overriding renderers was established by enumerating every ISpriteBatchRenderer implementation and grepping for the float overload (EasyGL, OPENGL4, SOFTWARE); GDI's sprite batch wraps the Software 2D core but forwards only the three integer overloads, so it inherits the truncating default too. Test coverage: SpriteBatchSubPixelDestinationTest in SpriteBatchTests.cpp checks that SpriteBatch records fractional positions. modules/graphics/examples/spritebatch_subpixel_contract_test.cpp (SOFTWARE-137) is a renderer-neutral, byte-exact pixel fixture (a direct float draw must equal an integer draw under a transform matrix, which a truncating renderer fails) and is registered only for EasyGL, OPENGL4 (parity corpus) and SOFTWARE; no other renderer registers it, so the truncating renderers have no sub-pixel pixel check.

refutation_attempt: Checked each renderer's SetImmediateMode use and the git history of every immediate flush. Found the OpenGL 4 flush came from a different commit (2026-09-24 rebuild) than the one cited, FNA3D's dates from its introduction, and a SOFTWARE-252 immediate-submission test the entry omits.
reason: The surviving gap is right: VULKAN, SDL_GPU, Direct3D and WEBGPU do not submit per Draw. But the commit attribution is wrong: 515958a7a fixed EasyGL only; OPENGL4 gained its flush in 50f3550a6 (2026-09-24) and FNA3D at introduction. Also spritebatch_immediate_submission_contract_test.cpp exists for EasyGL, OPENGL4 and SOFTWARE.
read: git history: 515958a7a, 50f3550a6, a9f817225 (ancestors of the TARGET commit)

correction.actual: CNA passes the mode to the renderer, and what the renderer does is per family. EasyGL flushes the sprite before Draw returns while immediate mode is set (its sprite Draw ends with if (immediateMode_) FlushBatch();, added by commit 515958a7a on 2026-09-09, SOFTWARE-252, an ancestor of TARGET). OPENGL4 has the same flush since its rebuild on EasyGL's semantics (commit 50f3550a6, 2026-09-24, GL4-0009 to GL4-0017, also an ancestor of TARGET). FNA3D has flushed in immediate mode since it was introduced (commit a9f817225, 2026-08-10), and SOFTWARE rasterises at once. VULKAN (it reads SetImmediateMode only in the compiled-effects build) and SDL_GPU (the same) record sprites for replay at present, and the Direct3D families and WEBGPU have no SetImmediateMode override, so they keep accumulating one run per texture until a texture change or End(); texture uploads take effect immediately. docs/xna-4-api-coverage.md records the Vulkan case as “Partial (divergent by decision)” with the measured cost of honouring it, but its statement that the divergence is CNA-wide, measured on EasyGL and Vulkan, predates SOFTWARE-252 and is stale for EasyGL. modules/graphics/examples/spritebatch_sort_mode_semantics_test.cpp documents the behaviour without asserting XNA's answer, and its header note that both measured renderers accumulate is likewise stale for EasyGL.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5, including the git history of each immediate flush; nothing was built or executed for this entry. Narrowed by the independent adversarial audit: the entry originally named EasyGL as a renderer that batches below the seam. Commit 515958a7a (2026-09-09, an ancestor of TARGET) made EasyGL honour immediate submission; OPENGL4 gained the same flush in its 2026-09-24 rebuild and FNA3D had it from its introduction. Direct3D, WebGPU, Vulkan and SDL_GPU behaviour was read in the same review (no SetImmediateMode override, or the mode read only under compiled effects). Tests: EasyGL_SpriteBatch_SortModeSemantics and Vulkan_SpriteBatch_SortModeSemantics check order and placement and leg D prices the alternative; none asserts the mid-batch texture-mutation result XNA gives. spritebatch_immediate_submission_contract_test.cpp (SOFTWARE-252) asserts immediate submission across a render-target switch and is registered for EasyGL, OPENGL4 and SOFTWARE only.

refutation_attempt: Searched all modules for another reader of the back-buffer usage (renderers, create args, manager, C API): only storage, cloning, equality; FNA3D hard-codes DISCARDCONTENTS. Confirmed in XNA's decompiled SetRenderTargets that the zero-target path consults it, and that CNA's does not.
reason: GraphicsDevice::SetRenderTargets reads only the first bound target's usage; the restore-to-back-buffer path never consults PresentationParameters.RenderTargetUsage, whereas XNA lazily clears on Discard. Unimplemented behaviour with no CNA statement promising it, matching sibling never-invoked-hook gaps, so gap class stands.

refutation_attempt: Traced SetData through TextureCube, the headless cube renderer and the XNB reader (refusal confirmed, deliberate, documented). Searched for a test that loads cube content on HEADLESS and found one asserting NotSupportedException on renderers without cube storage, contradicting the entry's claim that none exists.
reason: The gap is real and by design: the headless cube renderer stores nothing, TextureCube::SetData throws, and the XNB cube reader uploads per face and level. But the tests text is wrong: Texture3DTextureCubeContentTypeReaderTest loads a real cube XNB and pins NotSupportedException for HEADLESS, so the content consequence is asserted, not merely inferred.

correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry. The refusal is deliberate and documented in the header. Tests: Headless_CubeVolume_GetDataContract and Headless_CubeVolume_SetDataContract pin the refusal at renderer and TextureCube level. Texture3DTextureCubeContentTypeReaderTest.TextureCubeReaderLoadsRealMonoGameFixtureEndToEnd (modules/content/tests) loads a real cube XNB through ContentManager and, on renderers without cube storage (its gate lists SDL_RENDERER, CANVAS, HTML_DOM, FREEDIRECT, HEADLESS, GDI and PORTABLEGL), asserts System::NotSupportedException, so the loading consequence is pinned by CNA's own test whenever HEADLESS is the active renderer; the HEADLESS content CI job's test filter does not select that fixture.

refutation_attempt: Read every refusal site in MetalRenderer.mm, MetalPolicy.hpp capability and MSAA answers, the Metal tests and the macOS workflow. Looked for a lying capability flag (none: all refused features report false), for silent MSAA (it is reported as 0), and for tests touching the refusals.
reason: All refusals exist and are explicit, so the gap stands. Corrections: the sampler and blend refusals use plainer wording than the evidence-gated messages; MSAA is reported unsupported (capability false, applied count 0), not silent; and Metal_Capabilities and portable policy tests pin the refusals as reported, while a macOS CI job builds and runs the Metal tests.
read: modules/renderers/metal/src/MetalRenderer.mm::SetRenderTargets, CreateEffectRenderer, CreateOcclusionQuery, ReadBackbuffer, ApplySamplerMipState, ApplyBlendState, draw stream policy, ApplyMultiSampleCount, SpriteBatch SetCustomEffect

correction.actual: modules/renderers/metal/src/MetalRenderer.mm throws System::NotSupportedException, mostly with 'disabled until the adapted renderer has passing macOS ... evidence' wording, for: SetRenderTargets with more than one target; CreateEffectRenderer (ShaderEffect), SpriteBatch custom effects and custom-effect 3D draws; CreateOcclusionQuery; instancing and multi-stream vertex input; and ReadBackbuffer ('the historical macOS test run returned clear-color-only data after real draws'). It also throws, with plainer wording ('not implemented' and 'currently supports only'), for a sampler MaxMipLevel or MipMapLevelOfDetailBias other than 0 and for blend states with partial colour-write masks or a non-default MultiSampleMask. MetalAppliedMultiSampleCount in modules/renderers/metal/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Metal/MetalPolicy.hpp returns 0 for every request, so every MSAA request is clamped to none; this is reported rather than hidden (the MultiSampleAntiAliasing capability is false and the applied count is 0). MetalSupportsCapability reports false for MRT, occlusion queries, custom effects, multi-stream input and instancing, so the capability flags do not lie. The renderer builds only on macOS: the metal-macos-ci.yml workflow builds it on macos-14 and runs the ^Metal tests, while Linux hosts build only the portable policy tests.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry. The refusals are explicit and documented in the messages; macOS was not available. Tests: Metal_Capabilities asserts the refused features are reported unsupported, Metal_PortableHelpers pins the pure policy decisions (draw-stream policy, blend write state, applied MSAA count), and Metal_Smoke covers the supported contract (see CNA-VGAP-024); no test runs the throwing MetalRenderer paths themselves.

refutation_attempt: Searched CANVAS, FREEDIRECT and SDL_RENDERER sources and the SpriteBatch front end for any viewport or scissor override or other forwarding (none); confirmed GraphicsDevice forwards both; checked parity viewport fixture registrations (EasyGL, OPENGL4, WEBGPU, SDL_GPU only) and SDL_RENDERER docs, which claim only a round-trip.
reason: The interface defaults are empty, GraphicsDevice forwards viewport and scissor, and none of the three renderers overrides SetViewport (SDL_RENDERER overrides only scissor), so getters round-trip while drawing is unchanged. The unrelated depth-format sentence overlaps CNA-BUG-114 but is a cross-reference, not a duplicate.

refutation_attempt: Re-derived XNA's side by parsing the embedded XNA effect binaries in the decompiled reference: technique names equal the class names, WorldInverseTranspose is float3x3, Bones is float4x3[72]. Compared each CNA CacheEffectParameters table, the indexer's null result, the Effect constructors, docs and tests; found no compensation.
reason: All four CNA tables omit the texture and light parameters XNA caches, use 'Default' rather than XNA's per-effect technique name, and declare WorldInverseTranspose 4x4 and Bones as 72x4 where XNA has float3x3 and float4x3[72]. BasicEffect matches. No CNA doc promises generic parity, so gap class stands.

refutation_attempt: Looked for an owner check, lock or per-device registry (none; renderer destructors unregister by window id), a platform refusal to adopt one window twice (none), and input slots restored on teardown (only cleared when they still match). The registry test pins replace-on-register as intended.
reason: RegisterForWindow overwrites and UnregisterForWindow erases by window id with no owner check or lock, and createOrAttachWindow publishes each device's window to the process-wide TextInputEXT and Mouse slots, so the last writer wins. XNA's Mouse slot is also single, and distinct windows are unaffected, so this is a limited multi-device gap.

refutation_attempt: Grepped all three renderer trees for any read of the mode or virtual resolution beyond those cited (DIRECTX9 never reads them; CANVAS reads the mode only in getLogicalSize; FREEDIRECT stores it and letterboxes) and checked their docs. Only FREEDIRECT documents the limitation.
reason: FREEDIRECT stores the mode but its presenter always letterboxes (documented downgrade; also published as CNA-GAP-030), CANVAS special-cases only FixedHeightDynamicWidth, and DIRECTX9 assigns presentationMode_, virtualWidth_ and virtualHeight_ but never reads them, so every mode acts like native back buffer. Gap class stands.

refutation_attempt: Looked for another path registering volume textures (CreateTexture3D passes no registry, unlike CreateTextureCube), a CPU-mirror restore hook, and a doc calling this intended. The class has rawLevels_ for readback only; easygl_bugs.md lists it as missing. Context-loss tests cover other resources, not volumes.
reason: EasyGLTexture3DRenderer derives only from ITexture3DRenderer and CreateTexture3D omits the registry, while textures, cubes, targets, buffers and queries are RecoverableResources, so a context loss orphans volume handles. CNA's own bug ledger records it as missing, which makes it a documented limitation rather than an unknown defect.

refutation_attempt: Read the record-pass bracketing and closeOpenQuery3D, checked the quoted comment text, and compared XNA's decompiled OcclusionQuery (one Begin/End pair per count, so a single span crossing passes should sum). Looked for a sum-across-passes path or a contrary doc; none, and docs call it approved.
reason: Only the first contiguous run of a query's tagged draws per frame is bracketed; later runs, including in a later render pass, are never reopened because recordedThisFrame_ is set, so XNA's single-span count is undercounted. CNA's code comment and occlusion docs record this as an approved refusal, and the fixture covers one contiguous span.

refutation_attempt: Read CompileProgram (raw source to libshaderc, no version rewrite), the declared dialect and language support, and the fixture. Searched for CNA's own record of the refusal and found the measured libshaderc error text in the SDL_GPU plan, so the entry's 'not re-run' evidence understates it.
reason: The gap is right and deliberate: SDL_GPU declares SPIR-V, claims no GLSL, and CompileProgram hands GLSL straight to libshaderc, so the #version 300 es fixture cannot load. But the rejection is not just a reading: CNA's plan records the exact libshaderc errors, so evidence is recorded-by-CNA; #version 450 is one legal form, not the only one.

correction.actual: modules/renderers/sdl-gpu/src/SdlGpuRenderer.cpp's SdlGpuEffectRenderer::CompileProgram accepts SPIR-V words directly or, when built with CNA_SDL_GPU_SHADER_EFFECTS, passes GLSL source unchanged to libshaderc for Vulkan-rule SPIR-V and declares one uniform buffer per stage and one fragment sampler to SDL_gpu. The renderer declares ShaderDialectEXT::SpirV and claims no GLSL language, deliberately, because the GLSL ES 3.00 profile is not a legal input on that route. The fixture in modules/content/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Content/CnjEffectTests.cpp uses #version 300 es sources with a non-block uniform, which that route refuses; custom GLSL effects for SDL_GPU must follow Vulkan GLSL rules (for example #version 450) with explicit locations, uniform blocks and SDL_gpu's sets.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry. CNA's own plan (plans/plan_sdlgpu_modern_graphics.md) records the measured libshaderc refusal of the GLSL ES 3.00 profile on SDL_GPU (ES shaders for SPIR-V require version 310 or higher; SPIR-V requires location for user input/output; non-opaque uniforms outside a block are not allowed for Vulkan GLSL), and the fixture's sources use the same constructs. Tests: SDL_GPU's own ShaderEffect fixtures use #version 450; CnjEffectTests is not run against SDL_GPU in any workflow; its expectation predicate is published separately as CNA-BUG-204.
